unmapped_findings: The paper reports a dynamic recrystallization (DRX) state diagram (Fig. 7) dividing hot-deformation conditions into A work-hardening, B partial-DRX and C complete-DRX zones in the lnZ–strain plane; the critical strain εc and steady-state strain εs both increase with increasing lnZ (b0058, figure_007).

For this Fe-Mn-Al-C steel a fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained by hot working in the range 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1 (b0012, b0065, b0086); the specific 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1 condition of this sample is not listed among these optimum windows.

No optical micrograph is reported specifically at 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1; the Fig. 9 micrographs at 1050 °C were obtained at ε̇ = 1 s^-1 (panel e), and the Fig. 9 panels at ε̇ = 0.01 s^-1 were obtained at 1100 °C (panels a), so the microstructure image belonging to this exact sample is not available (b0060, b0063, figure_009).

The steel is reported as a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: rheological (flow) stress decreases with increasing T and with decreasing ε̇; the peak stress at ε̇ = 0.01 s^-1 decreased from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C (a reduction of 82%) (b0012, b0021, b0024, b0084).

Reproducibility of the compression experiments was checked using the same Fe-Mn-Al-C steel batch with the same composition under identical experimental conditions (b0018, b0021, b0024, b0037, b0058, b0065).

In the DRX average grain size vs temperature plot (Fig. 10) the grain size at every temperature ranks 0.01 s^-1 > 0.1 s^-1 > 1 s^-1 > 10 s^-1; at 1150 °C the 0.01 s^-1 curve reaches just below 80 µm while the 10 s^-1 curve stays near 20–25 µm, but no numeric value is printed for the 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1 point (figure_010, figure_011).
The paper discusses general conclusions and a 'prospect' section proposing future multivariate (experimental-design/chemometric) studies, with no sample-specific data (b0088, b0089, b0090).
